method: Manually cross-referenced (direct visual reading, not OCR/automated): (1) runner molded colors from the Parts List page (PDF p.3), (2) which runner+part-number callouts appear in which assembly step/section across the full instruction sequence (PDF pp.4-13, steps 1-16), and (3) the kit's PAINTING guide categories (PDF p.8, MSN-06S section only - the separate Full Frontal FIGURE paint guide on the same page is excluded on purpose per the user's request). A runner is mapped to a painting_guide category only when its parts were directly observed being used in that category's physical region of the model.
not_covered: This maps color/paint INTENT, not shape/geometry - it does not identify which pixels/contours in a diagram belong to which part. That would be a separate part-shape-isolation step.

thruster_yellow.label_ja: スラスターなどイエロー部の塗装色

sensor.label_ja: センサーなどの塗装色

bazooka_dark.label_ja: ロケット・バズーカの塗装色

trim_gold.label_ja: 袖、胸など装飾部の塗装色

bazooka_light.label_ja: ロケット・バズーカ、ライトグレー部の塗装色

A.note: Black is used for small spike/vent/accent shapes across nearly every section (head, body, arms, legs, shield), not one localized area. 'chest' (Midnight Blue, ~black) is the only near-black formula in the guide, so it's the best-fit existing recipe for all of A's parts, but Bandai doesn't explicitly say 'use this on A-runner parts' - this is an inference from color proximity.

B.note: Small yellow accent parts recur at multiple joint/vent locations (upper body, legs, waist) - consistent with the guide's single 'thruster/yellow parts' formula being used kit-wide wherever yellow accents appear, not just the backpack thrusters.

C.note: Directly confirmed: used for both the cockpit hatch/head sensor and the rifle scope lens - matches the guide's 'sensor' category exactly (translucent clear/blue/yellow green mix).

D.note: Outer armor-shell parts across head/waist/body - the kit's main red color, matches 'body' category directly.

E.note: Outer armor-shell parts for arms/legs/shield - same red as D, same category.

F.note: Outer armor-shell parts for arms/shoulders/upper body - same red category as D/E.

G.note: Outer armor-shell parts for legs/thighs - same red category as D/E/F.

H.note: Small connector/pipe-segment parts feeding into the flexible cable/pipe-spring assemblies - internal frame hardware, matches 'joint' category.

observed_in_sections: BACK PACK (10-1, 10-3) - the large wing-like thruster tube housings
I.note: NO dedicated category exists in the official painting guide for this. I-parts are exclusively the big backpack thruster tube shells. The closest formula by ingredient overlap is 'bazooka_light' (White 70% + Gray 30% + Purple, small amount), since it's also white-based, but that's a guess by color similarity, not a documented Bandai recommendation - do not treat as confirmed.

J.note: Used exclusively for the beam rifle body and its mounting hardware - directly matches the guide's 'weapon' (Navy Blue + Dark Green) category, distinct from the plain gray joint frame.

K.note: The core inner-frame/joint runner for body and waist, plus the axe's handle joint mechanism - consistent with 'joint' category throughout.

L.note: Inner-frame/joint parts for head, arms, and the shield's mounting frame - matches 'joint' category.

M.note: Inner-frame/joint parts for arms/upper body/backpack, plus the beam axe's blade-holder mechanism - matches 'joint' category.

observed_in_sections: LEGS (6-1 through 6-9, 7-1, 7-2) - entire leg inner frame
N.note: The leg inner-frame/joint runner - matches 'joint' category.

observed_in_sections: WEAPON EQUIPMENT (16-2 through 16-7) - large fin/blade-shaped attachment, likely the long-range sensor/effect part
O.note: NO dedicated category in the painting guide. This is a distinct translucent yellow effect/optic part, different from both the opaque 'thruster_yellow' formula and the clear-GREEN 'sensor' formula - neither is a documented match. Left unmapped rather than guessed.

P.note: Used exclusively for the bazooka. The guide gives TWO bazooka formulas (main dark gray + 'light gray part'), and the assembly diagrams don't call out which individual P-number is which shade - that distinction is a painter's judgment call by looking at the finished-kit photo, not something in the numbered instructions. Both categories apply somewhere within the P-parts group; this mapping can't resolve it further at the individual-part level from the manual alone.

unmapped_categories.trim_gold: No runner is molded gold. The 'sleeve/chest decorative' gold trim (label_en: trim_gold) is achieved via the kit's accessory stickers/decals (カラーシール/ガンダムデカール/マーキングシール, listed on the Parts List page) and/or hand-painting over red/black parts - not a distinct plastic runner.
